content.title: About
content.content: Ramen soup is a traditional Japanese dish consisting of wheat‑flour noodles served in a flavorful broth. This version includes water added to the dry noodle packet, allowing a quick, complete ramen to be prepared at home.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ramen originated in China but became popular in Japan in the early 20th century.
Dry ramen kits often contain spices, dried vegetables, and meat pieces.
The added water activates gluten in the noodles, giving them a firm, chewy texture.
There are more than 30 regional broth styles: shoyu, miso, shio, and tonkotsu.
In Japan ramen is considered street food, and many cities have dedicated ramen bars.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Ramen noodles provide fast‑acting carbs that quickly replenish energy.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Dry mixes often include dried chicken or pork protein, boosting the protein content.

items.title: Minerals from broth
items.content: Seasoning packets can supply sodium, potassium, and magnesium, important for electrolyte balance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour and spices provide modest amounts of B1, B2, and niacin.

items.title: Convenient preparation
items.content: Adding water and a short boil yields a hot meal in minutes, ideal for time‑pressed situations.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Dry ramen kits are often very salty, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Wheat‑based noodles are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Additives and flavor enhancers
items.content: Some kits contain artificial flavors and MSG, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑rich, especially when topped with fatty ingredients.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bring 500 ml of water to a boil, add the dry noodles and cook for 3‑4 minutes. Then stir in the seasoning packet and let sit for 1‑2 minutes. Optionally top with a boiled egg, sliced green onions, nori, or meat slices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry ramen kit in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer to an airtight container to prevent moisture absorption.
